issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance, after the Task 3 pilots pre-guessed numbers GitHub then allocated elsewhere.
hypothesis: The trainable-scope comparison showed that lifting the Task 3 freeze converts strong-opponent experience into a better tournament agent - full fine-tuning beat the frozen arm by 1.43 score with the interval excluding zero - but that the same arm failed the registered retention gates on loot-crate and classic-peaceful. Scope was binary there, so that comparison cannot say whether the forgetting is inherent to fine-tuning or is a function of how far each update moves the inherited weights. This comparison varies the learning rate alone over three doses at a fixed all_weights scope. If forgetting scales with step size while the tournament gain does not, a reduced dose is promotable and the campaign has a usable agent. If both scale together, the trade-off is inherent to this scope and the next lever is rehearsal of earlier-task experience rather than a smaller step.

prior_evidence.trainable_scope_result: Six replicas per arm, 400 episodes each. Against three rule_based_agents the all_weights arm scored 2.650 against the frozen arm's 1.221 and the unchanged incumbent's 2.350; survival 0.458 against 0.125 and 0.300; self-kills 0.462 against 0.825 and 0.625. Against the incumbent the gain was +0.30 with the interval [-0.546, +1.113], so it is not established. Retention failed: loot-crate collection 0.228 to 0.166 for the fine-tuned arm, classic-peaceful 0.331 to 0.242 for it and to 0.071 for the frozen arm.
prior_evidence.frozen_regime: Training under the frozen scope was significantly worse than not training at all on score, collection, survival and self-kills. The frozen regime is not a candidate here and is not carried as an arm.
prior_evidence.dose_response_precedent: The Task 3 opponent-shrinkage comparison established the analysis pattern: a monotone response across a registered dose ladder is interpretable evidence about the mechanism, and a flat response is evidence against it.

intervention.changed_factor: the optimizer learning rate, over a registered three-point ladder
intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: the installed Task 3 incumbent as the starting point, the all_weights trainable scope, three rule_based_agents as the training line-up, native rewards with no approach shaping, one optimizer update per eligible transition and the #168 episode-mixture exploration schedule
intervention.persistence: training-only; evaluation loads the unchanged archived agent
intervention.registered_risk: The control arm reproduces the dose that already failed retention, so at least one arm is expected to fail the retention gates. That is the point of the ladder and is not grounds for relaxing them afterwards. A reduced dose that holds retention only by learning nothing is caught by the efficacy gates, which require a gain over the unchanged incumbent rather than mere safety.

random_episode_schedule: All arms: for each five-episode block random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(5) selects one fully random episode; four greedy episodes.
primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on classic-rule-based against the unchanged incumbent. Tournament placing is decided by score, so score rather than eliminations is the endpoint this campaign is built to move.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per treatment arm that can be promoted; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: An arm is promotable only if every integrity gate, every retention gate and every efficacy gate passes. Among promotable arms the largest mean score gain over the unchanged incumbent is chosen, and within it the median-final replica by that score. The best-looking replica is not selectable. If no arm is promotable the installed incumbent remains the submission candidate.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this exploratory comparison cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: The zero-invalid-action gate counts the unchanged reference's own invalid actions, so no arm could pass it in the Task 3 programme. It is retained unchanged and is expected to fail; read it alongside the per-artifact counts rather than as a discriminator between arms. The frozen_online_weights integrity gate is likewise expected to fail for every arm here, because every arm registers the all_weights scope whose registered purpose is to move those weights.

machine_allocation.training: 5 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source

authorization: Owner 1BlauNitrox requested and authorized this comparison on 15 September 2026 as the registered follow-up to the completed trainable-scope comparison, to be prepared and started unattended on the PC. One registered comparison per host, no automatic extension, no automatic promotion; the README and interpretation follow completed results.
